title: Anyone who may change settings edits the email sender's mailboxes, postal address, sending hours and caps from Settings, instead of writing senders/email.json on the machine
description: FW-C-094 shows whether the email sender is set up, but its settings file ($FW_HOME/senders/email.json) is still written by hand on the machine. fwd takes POST /v1/connections/email from the CLI token or a paired browser session with { mailboxes: [{ key, address, name }] (1 to 3, key a-z0-9_ starting with a letter, unique), postal (required, at most 300 characters), daily_cap (1 to 40), per_pass (1 to 5), hours: { start (0 to 23), end (1 to 24, after start), days (0 to 6, at least one) } }, checks it the way senders/email.mjs does, and writes the file atomically with mode 0600: those fields are replaced, every other key (routes, claim, smtp_url) is kept, a route to a mailbox that no longer exists is dropped, and frequency is routed to the first mailbox when no route names it. A body that carries a password, secret or token field is refused: passwords stay in the keychain. GET /v1/connections returns email.values (mailboxes, postal, daily_cap, per_pass, hours, or null with no file). The site queues it as kind connection.email (flow all; hosted/server/requests.mjs; migration 0008 allows the kind and every kind 0007 allowed) and the relay calls the same route. In Settings, Connections, Email sending gets Edit: address and name per mailbox, postal address, daily cap, per pass, start and end hour and days, and Save; no password field; read only for people who may not change it. Tokens only. No em dashes.
acceptance: POST /v1/connections/email from a browser session writes the sender's settings and keeps routes, claim and smtp_url
A route to a removed mailbox is dropped and frequency is routed to the first mailbox
Out-of-range caps, hours, days, a bad address, an empty postal address and a password field are refused with 400
The site queues connection.email with a checked payload, the relay calls the same route, and migration 0008 allows the kind
Settings edits and saves the sender's settings, has no password field, and is read only for people who may not change it
